title: Speaker-Specific and Language-Dependent Temporal Organization in Bilingual Political Speech
abstract: arXiv:2609.16274v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speech rhythm helps structure persuasive speech, but most empirical work examines monolingual English. This study asks how politicians organize timing when speaking Luxembourgish and French. We analyze 400 sentences from ten politicians, annotated for segments and pauses. We compute rhythm metrics, including means, variability, and pairwise variability indices for consonants and vowels. We quantify speaker and language contributions and test within-speaker language effects with paired t-tests. Results show that consonant-based metrics retain speaker-specific signatures, whereas vowel-based metrics are largely driven by language choice. French tokens display longer and more variable vowels and vocalic intervals, while consonant timing differences are smaller. No robust language by gender interactions emerge. These findings show that language choice systematically reorganizes rhythmic timing in bilingual public speech.

translated_title: 双语政治演讲中特定说话者与语言依赖的时间组织
translated_abstract: 语音节奏有助于构建有说服力的演讲，但大多数实证研究仅考察单语英语。本研究探讨政治家在说卢森堡语和法语时如何组织时间节奏。我们分析了来自十位政治家的400个句子，并对音段和停顿进行了标注。我们计算了节奏指标，包括辅音和元音的均值、变异性和成对变异性指数。我们量化了说话者和语言的贡献，并通过配对t检验测试了说话者内部的语言效应。结果表明，基于辅音的指标保留了说话者特有的签名特征，而基于元音的指标主要由语言选择驱动。法语的元音和元音区间更长且更多变，而辅音时间差异较小。研究未发现稳健的语言与性别交互效应。这些发现表明，语言选择会系统地重组双语公共演讲中的节奏时间组织。
tldr: 本研究通过分析政治家的卢森堡语和法语双语演讲发现，辅音节奏指标保留说话者个人特征，而元音节奏指标主要由语言选择驱动，表明语言选择会系统性重组双语公共演讲的节奏时间组织。
en_tdlr: Analyzing bilingual political speech in Luxembourgish and French, this study reveals that consonant-based rhythm metrics retain speaker-specific signatures while vowel-based metrics are largely driven by language choice, demonstrating that language choice systematically reorganizes rhythmic timing in bilingual public speech.
